title: Commit Harmony: tiered burst credits + predictive autoscale pricing experiment
creator: Sofia Morales
description: Run an experiment to replace the current monolithic reserved-GPU SKU with a multi-tiered committed offering that blends baseline reserved capacity, transparent burst credits, and a predictive autoscale add-on. Goals: simplify enterprise procurement conversations, reduce overcommit discounts, give predictable unit economics for engineering teams, and ensure contract language maps cleanly to security questionnaire answers.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 pricing tiers (Baseline, Elastic, Enterprise Burst) with unit price per reserved GPU-hour and burst credit buckets
Build a predictive autoscale pricing model that uses customer historical burn-rate to recommend commit levels and expected burst usage
Legal / Sales-approved contract language and SOW snippet that aligns with customers' security questionnaire requirements
Pilot with 2 existing dedicated customers and measure delta in committed revenue and churn risk compared to current offers
Console shows transparent per-route cost breakdown including burst credit consumption and autoscale triggers
updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff with Product, Sales, Legal, and Eng. Agreed scope: pricing tiers + burst credit mechanics + autoscale recommendation engine MVP.
2026-02-25: Sales provided 6 anonymised customer portfolios for modeling; initial revenue uplift estimate +6-12% for mid-market profiles.
2026-03-03: Engineering feasibility sync - runtime telemetry required for burst credit reconciliation (ENG-4021). ETA for telemetry schema: 2026-03-24.
2026-03-05: Legal reviewed draft contract clauses; raised two outstanding items around force-majeure and cross-region failover obligations needing precise SLA language.
2026-03-09: Design reviewed billing UX. Decided to surface 'burn rate forecast' and 'recommended commit' on the dedicated SKU page; initial mockups in Drive linked below.
2026-03-10: PM scoped pilot customers: AcmeRetail (mid-market) and NovaHealth (enterprise). Sales outreach started; expected pilot start 2026-04-07.
decisions: Adopt a credit-first burst model (credits consumed before overage billing) to simplify reconciliation for customers.
Expose an explicit predictive commit recommendation to customers but keep opt-in autoscale as a paid add-on.
Bundle basic observability for burst consumption into all tiers; advanced retention is an add-on.
Map contract SLA tiers to predictable latency percentiles and to a separate pool for burst capacity (documentation to avoid cross-dependency claims).
tradeoffs: Giving credits upfront improves customer confidence but reduces short-term revenue recognition compared to pure overage billing.
Predictive autoscale improves unit economics but increases product complexity and requires additional telemetry (engineering cost).
Tighter SLA guarantees drive sales for enterprise but require capacity reservation that increases operational cost if adoption is low.
